transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-28 | Start: 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~82 mins
Attendees: Laura, Marcus, Ivy, Samir, Nora, Ethan, Priya, Jonas, Rina

Summary: Quick technical postmortem of the 11:14 incident, then roadmap actions to harden runtime and stop regressions from kernel changes and quantization patches. Focus areas: canary gating, regression tests, KV cache evictions, and fallback behaviors.

Topics: runtime regressions; kernel fallback; quantization variance; nightly smoke tests; release windows; runbook clarity.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Laura Chen: Okay, good afternoon everyone, thanks for carving time. high level agenda — two parts: quick incident recap then workshop on guardrails for the runtime. Marcus, can you kick off with the timeline?
[00:22] Marcus Patel: Yeah sure. so timeline — 11:14 we started seeing token delays and a spike in latency for 4xxs on the inference fleet, root cause ended up being a kernel selector change that interacted poorly with long context LRU heuristic, basically kv cache churn.
[00:43] Nora Blake: sorry to interrupt, Marcus — kv cache churn meaning eviction frequency shot up?
[00:49] Marcus Patel: exactly, eviction rate 3x for sequences above 3k tokens, so our prefix cache missed more often and that increased compute and queuing.
[01:05] Ethan Morris: we also saw increased OOMs on a small subset of machines, not universal, which made the autoscaler trigger scale events and that amplified queuing.
[01:20] Ivy Gonzalez: can we be explicit: this was a selector change in the kernel optimizer that was rolled last Thursday in canary then partially to prod?
[01:31] Marcus Patel: correct — the canary metrics didn't catch the long-tail because our smoke tests sample short sequences and quantized models.
[01:44] Priya Kapoor: and to add — quantization replay on the traces showed higher memory allocations in the new kernel path; it's subtle, maybe alignment differences.
[01:58] Jonas Lee: QA missed it because we don't have a nightly that runs long-context prompts end-to-end with exact kv behavior, our tests truncated at 2k tokens historically.
[02:12] Samir Rao: this is a systemic gap: kernel/compile changes are low risk in short seqs but high risk on long seq production patterns. we need a guardrail pipeline.

[02:30] Laura Chen: Agreed. Workshop portion — brainstorm concrete guardrails: canary gating changes, regression suites, runtime telemetry thresholds, and runbook clarifications. Marcus, propose a minimal set.
[02:50] Marcus Patel: proposal A: expand nightly smoke matrix to include: 1) long-context synthetic traces (3k–8k tokens) 2) a replay of 100 production traces sampled from last 24h across customers 3) quantization replay for our top 5 models. run these on a small dedicated canary fleet prior to rollout.
[03:15] Priya Kapoor: For quantization replay: we need deterministic replay — capture mem profiles and full KV cache behavior not just outputs. that will catch alignment-induced allocations.
[03:29] Ethan Morris: Also add a memory-saturation test: gradually increase concurrent sessions to target p90 and watch eviction policies. This will surface autoscaler coupling.
[03:42] Ivy Gonzalez: on gating, proposal B: block merges with kernel-selector changes from auto-release unless the canary fleet passes the expanded suite for 48 hours and p99 latency delta < 10% on long traces.
[03:59] Rina Takahashi: we'll need an SLA for how long canaries can run; 48h might be long for some patches. propose a fast-path for urgent security fixes with stricter rollback criteria.
[04:16] Marcus Patel: okay, so two paths: normal path 48h + suite, urgent path immediate rollout but with feature flag + 6h close monitoring and immediate auto-rollback if p99 degrades >15%.
[04:32] Nora Blake: sounds reasonable. who owns automating the p99 check?
[04:38] Marcus Patel: SRE but needs telemetry hooks from runtime team — small change to expose kernel path tag in traces. Priya and Compiler team to add tag.

[04:52] Priya Kapoor: quick note: adding tags won't be free, but it's small. we should be careful about sampling overhead. suggest sample rate 1% for now.
[05:03] Samir Rao: on the infra side, we'll provision a tiny canary pool of identical hw shapes to prod so results are comparable. also add a KV-cache instrumentation dashboard.
[05:17] Jonas Lee: QA will own the nightly expansion and add test flakiness guards. I'm concerned about test runtime; long traces will increase runtime — we might need to parallelize tests.
[05:29] Marcus Patel: we can parallelize by model shards and cap concurrency. the goal is representative, not exhaustive.

[05:43] Laura Chen: let's talk about runbook and incident response changes. Jonas, what do you want in the postmortem skeleton?
[05:50] Jonas Lee: timeline, detection signals, initial mitigations, root cause, cross-team decisions, and concrete follow-ups. add a short 'how to triage' appendix for pq (prefix-queue) specific issues — what to check first: eviction rates, kernel tag, memory alloc rates.
[06:10] Ethan Morris: also add a checklist for rolling back kernel selector changes safely — e.g., drain canary fleet, promote rollback image, monitor 10 minutes, then continue.
[06:21] Priya Kapoor: we should add a regression label to PRs that modifies kernel/selectors so QA knows to run long-context tests automatically.

[06:35] Laura Chen: good. now risk mitigation for release windows — Rina?
[06:40] Rina Takahashi: propose two-week maintenance windows in January 2027 with one 48h window for low-risk work and one 72h for larger infra changes; also propose a policy that kernel/compile changes require at least one maintenance window unless urgent.
[06:58] Nora Blake: two-week windows are fine but we need business alignment. Ivy, can you flag major partners and customers for notification?
[07:07] Ivy Gonzalez: yes I'll compile a list and recommend communication cadence. also propose a scheduled 'runtime health drill' with the customer success and SRE teams mid-Jan.

[07:20] Marcus Patel: technical nit — fallback behavior: we need an explicit, tested path where if kernel path A fails we fall back to kernel path B with a controlled perf penalty but stable memory. current fallback was manual. we should automated it.
[07:37] Priya Kapoor: agree. we'll need to keep the older kernel binary around for hot fallback and add a small check inside the runtime to detect pathological memory usage and switch.
[07:47] Samir Rao: infra will mark the fallback image as compatible and add an automated toggle in the orchestrator, plus a circuit breaker on autoscaler to avoid cascading scale.

[08:00] Jonas Lee: testing fallback will be tricky — we'll add synthetic fault injection to canaries to force fallback and validate correctness.

[08:15] Laura Chen: let's capture the instrumentation and dashboard asks: KV cache eviction rate, per-kernel memory delta, p50/p90/p99 for long traces, autoscaler churn, OOM counts. Marcus?
[08:27] Marcus Patel: yes, central dashboard. also add 'kernel-path' tag to traces and a leaderboard of worst-performing traces so we can triage quickly.

[08:40] Nora Blake: a couple of questions from PM team: how will this affect release velocity long term? are we adding too much friction?
[08:48] Ivy Gonzalez: short term yes, we slow down to avoid outages. long term the expanded suite and automation will speed recovery and reduce rework — net positive.

[09:02] Rina Takahashi: logistics: Rina to propose actual January windows, Marcus to size canary fleet and storage, Priya to update compiler tagging RFC, Jonas to prep postmortem skeleton.

[09:20] Laura Chen: wrap-up — recap of decisions: 1) expand nightly/regression suite to include long-context and quant replay 2) canary gating (48h normal, urgent fast-path with rollback criteria) 3) automated fallback path and orchestrator toggle 4) instrumentation tags and dashboards 5) postmortem and triage checklist.

[09:45] Jonas Lee: quick callouts — I'll include a short appendix in the postmortem with command list for triage and a minimal runbook for SRE on kernel events.
[09:58] Marcus Patel: I'll draft the regression checklist and the smoke matrix and put it in the team's confluence space.
[10:08] Priya Kapoor: I'll run quant replay on the failing traces today and post initial variance report.
[10:19] Rina Takahashi: I'll circulate window options and draft release comms.
[10:30] Ivy Gonzalez: I'll update the canary criteria doc and coordinate partner notifications.

[10:40] Laura Chen: any other risks?
[10:44] Ethan Morris: just one — we should watch for test flakiness causing false positives that delay releases, need an escape hatch.
[10:52] Samir Rao: escape hatch is documented: urgent security path with stricter monitoring and auto-rollback; plus a small human-in-loop approval for high-risk patches.

[11:05] Laura Chen: great. meeting adjourned. thanks everyone.
